calib_q.note: one stage per quantity (binding q); Table 1 order (derived: the paper says only that 'The quantities appeared in the same order in all questionnaires', p. 1163)

anch_q.note: 'three consecutive questions about each of the 15 quantities' (p. 1162): judgment, estimate, confidence on one stage per quantity (binding q; page layout derived). The anchor shown is data.items[q][low|high] (Table 1) per the per-session anchor draw; it is part of the missing judgment text

fields.extreme: None if est is None else ((est > anchor) if dir == 'high' else (est < anchor))
fields.consistent: None if est is None or judg is None or est == anchor else ((est > anchor) == (judg == 'gt'))

fields.conf_mean: mean([answer('calib_q.conf', q=q) for q in data['item_ids']]) if arm == 'calib' else mean([answer('anch_q.conf', q=q) for q in data['item_ids']])
fields.ext_high: None if arm != 'anch' else mean([(1 if answer('anch_q.est', q=q) > data['items'][q]['high'] else 0) for q in data['item_ids'] if dirs[data['idx'][q]] == 'high' and answer('anch_q.est', q=q) is not None])
fields.ext_low: None if arm != 'anch' else mean([(1 if answer('anch_q.est', q=q) < data['items'][q]['low'] else 0) for q in data['item_ids'] if dirs[data['idx'][q]] == 'low' and answer('anch_q.est', q=q) is not None])

Mean confidence rating: anchored group minus calibration group

unsupported.what: transformed (percentile) estimates, high vs low anchors: medians 76 vs 36, t(102) = 7.99, p < .01 (p. 1163); Table 1 'Transformed Medians'
unsupported.why: needs each anchored estimate converted to its percentile in the calibration group's distribution (a cross-arm transform; ties/out-of-range rules: 'assigned values of 100 or 0', p. 1162); the engine has no such unit field (meta.engine_requests.calibration_percentile)

unsupported.what: Anchoring Index per problem (Table 1) and its means: overall .49, high .51, low .40 (p. 1163); highly-confident quartile AI .28 (p. 1165)
unsupported.why: a ratio of group medians and anchors: covered by the median targets (AI = (Mdn high - Mdn low) / (high - low), reproduced from the printed medians to 2 places by build_protocol.py); not a separate scored quantity. The confident-quartile AI needs a per-problem 25% split on confidence

unsupported.what: mean point-biserial correlation of estimate and anchor over the 15 problems, .42 (p. 1163)
unsupported.why: an average of 15 item-level correlations (item-level aggregate; engine request item_aggregates)

unsupported.what: correlation between AI and mean calibration confidence over the 15 problems, -.68, p < .05 (p. 1165)
unsupported.why: a correlation across items (n = 15) of item-level statistics (engine request item_aggregates)

unsupported.what: mean within-problem correlation of transformed estimate and confidence: -.14 for high anchors (t(14) = 2.37, p < .05), .27 for low anchors (t(14) = 4.80, p < .001) (p. 1165)
unsupported.why: needs the percentile transform and item-level aggregation (engine requests)

unsupported.what: confident vs less confident subjects' medians closer to the truth on 8 of 15 problems, farther on 5, equal on 2 (p. 1165)
unsupported.why: needs the true values (not given in the paper) and a per-problem confidence split

unsupported.what: the 'close replication ... with an added manipulation intended to discredit' the anchor (28% / 15%) and Green, Jacowitz, Kahneman & McFadden (1995) WTP study (p. 1164)
unsupported.why: other experiments, only summarised here; not part of this paper's study (the legacy build's exp_2_discredited_anchor / exp_3_wtp_estimation were dropped)

keyed.why: paper's pattern (scratch unblocked copy only; both arms blocked): high anchors judged low and exceeded more often than low anchors are undershot; estimates follow the judgment; anchored subjects more confident

answers.anch_q.judg: 'gt' if ((1.2 if data['idx'][q] % 3 else 0.9) if dirs[data['idx'][q]] == 'high' else (0.8 if data['idx'][q] % 3 == 0 else 1.2)) > 1 else 'lt'
answers.anch_q.est: data['items'][q][dirs[data['idx'][q]]] * ((1.2 if data['idx'][q] % 3 else 0.9) if dirs[data['idx'][q]] == 'high' else (0.8 if data['idx'][q] % 3 == 0 else 1.2))
